description: Roblox performance - designing systems that scale and diagnosing or fixing lag, with evidence-tagged rules for Luau, memory and garbage collection, buffers and serialization, networking and replication, instances and pooling, physics and moving parts, rendering, and UI. Load it before designing a system that runs per frame, handles many entities or instances, or fires remotes often; when the user reports lag, low FPS, stutter, high ping, memory growth, crashes on phones, slow joins, UI that flickers or draws blank, or sounds that play late; when asked to optimize, profile, or benchmark anything in a place; and before adding pooling, buffers, a networking library, Parallel Luau, or native code generation for speed. Load it even when the optimization looks obvious, because its first job is deciding whether to optimize at all.

results.query: With 12 players building, everyone's ping climbs to 400 ms. How do I find out what's flooding the network?
Once my build has about 5,000 blocks the game drops to around 30 FPS on my phone. Where do I even start?
I'm making a gun that fires 600 rounds a minute. Should I pool the bullet parts or just Instance.new and Destroy them?
Design a server system for 300 chickens that wander around the farm map. It needs to not lag.
Server memory keeps climbing over a three-hour session, and phone players crash after about an hour. What usually causes that?
Add @native to my terrain generation module so it runs faster.
Players say joining our map takes 40 seconds. How can I make joins faster?
In my place, benchmark whether moving 2,000 parts with BulkMoveTo or by setting CFrame is cheaper.
Is it worth switching my projectile remote to send a buffer instead of a Vector3 and a number?
The click sound on my Vide shop button plays a beat late the first time anyone presses it.
